Verdict `support` when the quotes alone state every part of the claim and of each value, with the same scope and qualifiers; `partial` when a part is missing; `not-supported` when the quotes say something else; `unsure` otherwise. A quote with a `heading` is the value line under that heading on the page: read the two together. Do not use what you remember. A clause, scope, condition or exception of the claim that appears only in the surrounding text and not in the quotes is missing: `partial`. A universal claim (always, every, each, all) whose exception stands in the surrounding text is `partial`. When the quotes support the claim but you can see a sentence that would support it better, still vote on the quotes you were given.

#### Can I try Quick for free?
Amazon Quick offers a free trial option for new customers wanting to try the Enterprise plan:
| Trial duration | Users covered | What’s waived |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 days | Up to 25 users per account | Subscription fee + infrastructure fee waived |
During the 30-day free trial period:
- The full subscription fee is waived for up to 25 users
- The $250 infrastructure fee is waived for the account
- Customers can access all Enterprise Features. At the end of 30 days, customers with an AWS account will start being billed for an Enterprise plan.
- No credit card required to begin
headings: Can I try Quick for free?

evidence.title: Setting up a VPC to use with Amazon Quick
evidence.quote: To set up a VPC to use with Amazon Quick Enterprise edition, you need access to Amazon VPC and Amazon EC2.
evidence.context:
|  | 
| --- |
|    Intended audience:  System administrators  | 

To set up a VPC to use with Amazon Quick Enterprise edition, you need access to Amazon VPC and Amazon EC2. You also need access to each AWS database service that you plan to add to Quick. You can use the console, or you can use the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI). For more information about the CLI, see the [AWS Command Line Interface User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/). To work with the CLI, go to [https://aws.amazon.com/cli/](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/).

Before you begin to set up your VPC connection in Amazon Quick, make sure that you understand the components of a VPC deployment. As part of that, familiarize yourself with the VPC's subnets and security groups in relation to the destinations (databases) that you want to reach from Amazon Quick. To set up a successful VPC connection, make sure that the following components work together to allow network traffic to pass between Amazon Quick and your data source:
+ The Amazon VPC service
+ The subnets that your data source is using
+ The Amazon Quick elastic network interfaces and the subnets they use
headings: Setting up a VPC to use with Amazon Quick
